headline: Low interaction risk overall: EMQX can egress over HTTP, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no filesystem, network, or tool-use surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. agent_a is EMQX with HTTP API and broad network egress, while agent_b is a documentation-only content-writing artifact with no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or MCP. Without a shared channel, agent_a cannot inject instructions into agent_b by default.
conditions: IF agent_b is connected to a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue with agent_a, reassess as non-none.
IF an orchestrator begins piping agent_a output into agent_b prompts, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not route EMQX output directly into the writer's prompt.
Use explicit human review before copying content between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches IoT data and has broad egress, but agent_b has no network egress, no file access, and no declared data classes. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, so a leakage path from agent_a to agent_b is not evidenced in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same shared workspace with sensitive files, reassess upward.
IF agent_b gains network egress or file-reading capability, reassess upward.
mitigations: Run the writer in a no-network environment.
Keep IoT data out of any shared directory.
Separate credentials and principals for each agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. agent_a exposes HTTP API and broad network egress, but no filesystem or git write capability is listed; agent_b explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. The pair therefore lacks a documented mutable-resource conflict.
conditions: IF agent_a is deployed with filesystem or git write privileges not shown here, reassess upward.
IF a shared mutable resource is introduced via orchestration, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid granting shared write access to the same directory.
Keep git operations outside both agents.
Use a lock or single-writer policy if a shared resource is later added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can emit networked IoT-related outputs, but agent_b is documentation-only content writing and has no action-taking or API surfaces. The main risk is manual over-trust if a human copies agent_a output into agent_b; there is no default automated cascade from agent_a into agent_b.
conditions: IF an orchestrator automatically feeds agent_a output into agent_b as authoritative input, reassess upward.
IF agent_b is repurposed to execute actions from generated text, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require a verification step before reusing EMQX output.
Label agent_a output as untrusted source material.
Keep agent_b in drafting-only mode, not action mode.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. agent_a touches IoT data and has broad egress, while agent_b touches no data classes and has no network or file surfaces. The profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, residency constraints, or retention differences, so a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into the pair, reassess upward.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy not shown here, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention and residency rules before deployment.
Review whether any future data class requires a DPA or HIPAA controls.
